evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/neighbors/hooks/useNeighbors.ts:117 — useNeighbors memoes `getNeighborsApiClient()` with [] deps; api is captured once at mount with the token present then

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/neighbors/hooks/useNeighbors.ts:138 — usePrivacySettings has the same [] deps pattern; the api that drives both the read + the update mutation is pinned to the mount-time token

frontend/packages/api-client/src/neighbors/api.ts:30 — createNeighborsApi() calls buildHeaders(config) ONCE and freezes the Bearer-token `Authorization` header into every subsequent listNeighbors / getPrivacySettings / updatePrivacySettings fetch; this is raw fetch, so there is no axios interceptor to re-inject the rotated token

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/messaging/hooks/useMessaging.ts:402 — contrast: useMessageRecipients uses the SAME getNeighborsApi factory but memoes with [token] deps, so a token rotation rebuilds the api; useNeighbors.ts omits this and leaves consumers wedged on the stale token
signals.severity_rationale: +2 because: silent background token refresh is the common path for a long-lived SPA session, and once it happens every fetch and the privacy-settings update mutation on this hook pair will 401 against the raw fetch (no axios 401-replay interceptor on this transport), until the component unmounts. Not +3 because the component may re-mount on route navigation and the user can usually recover by refreshing.

evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/iot/hooks/useIotWebSocket.ts:54-60 — hook's return type documents `hasGivenUp` as the dedicated signal for 'reconnect budget exhausted, UI should surface explicit offline/retry affordance'
frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/iot.tsx:85 — only consumer destructures `{ liveReadings, isConnected }`; hasGivenUp is dropped on the floor

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/iot.tsx:153 — downstream IotDashboardPage receives only `isLive={isConnected}`, which collapses 'temporarily reconnecting' and 'permanently gave up' into the same UI state
signals.severity_rationale: +1 — not a correctness bug, but defeats the intent of the recent reconnect-cap fix (hook exposes `hasGivenUp` so UI can surface a manual-reconnect affordance; UI never reads it). Buffer refill only.

evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/auth/TwoFactorScreen.tsx:40 — handleVerify() only runs a client-side regex `/^\d{6}$/` on the entered code, then on pass immediately setStep('enabled'); there is NO backend enrollment or TOTP-verification call anywhere in the component

frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/auth/TwoFactorScreen.tsx:99 — step==='enabled' renders the copy 'Two-factor authentication is enabled.' purely from that local regex check, so ANY 6-digit number tells the user 2FA is active when nothing was registered server-side (false sense of account security)

frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/auth/TwoFactorScreen.tsx:76 — the verify step's help text instructs the user to 'Scan the QR code in your authenticator app', but no QR code / otpauth secret is ever rendered or fetched — there is nothing to scan, so a user who follows the instructions enrolls an unrelated/garbage TOTP seed

frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/auth/TwoFactorScreen.tsx:4 — the component docstring itself admits 'The backend endpoints for enrollment aren't exposed through our mobile auth layer yet, so this screen wires up local state' — i.e. the whole flow is a UI scaffold shipped as if functional
signals.severity_rationale: +3 because this is a security-feature correctness defect with a misleading user-facing outcome: the screen affirmatively claims 2FA is enabled on the account when zero server-side enrollment occurred, and directs the user to scan a QR code that does not exist. A user relying on this believes their account is hardened when it is not. candidate_vector=bug: either wire the real enroll/verify endpoints or gate the screen behind a 'coming soon' state so it cannot report a false enabled status. Confidence medium (static): did not confirm the navigation entry point that routes a production user into this screen.

evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/messages/MessagesScreen.tsx:125 — `placeholder="Search messages…"` is a hardcoded English literal, not wrapped in t(); the app ships sk/cs/de/en and this string will never localize

frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/meters/MeterReadingScreen.tsx:234 + frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/auth/LoginScreen.tsx:93 — contrast: peer screens correctly use t('meters.readingPlaceholder') / t('auth.emailPlaceholder'), so these two are regressions against the established pattern
signals.severity_rationale: +1 i18n gap: user-facing search placeholders stay English in Slovak/Czech/German locales. Low severity, purely localization polish; mechanical fix (add keys + wrap in t()).

evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/auth/{LoginScreen,RegisterScreen,ForgotPasswordScreen,TwoFactorScreen,AuthFlow}.tsx — none of these auth-screen components have a sibling *.test.tsx; the only auth coverage is frontend/apps/mobile/src/test/integration/auth.integration.test.tsx

frontend/apps/mobile/src/test/integration/auth.integration.test.tsx:127 — that suite exercises AuthContext logic (login/logout/refresh/biometric/cross-user cache reset) but renders none of the screen components, so the screens' own branches (validation, error display, step transitions) are untested

frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/auth/TwoFactorScreen.tsx:38 — concretely, the TwoFactorScreen idle→verify→enabled state machine and its 6-digit validation error path have zero test coverage, which is how the stub-success defect (see code-review-mobile-rn-twofactor-stub-false-enabled) shipped unnoticed
signals.severity_rationale: +1 test gap on security-sensitive screens. Not higher because AuthContext (the stateful core) is well-covered by the integration suite; the gap is the presentational screen branches. A render-level test on each would also have caught the 2FA false-enabled path.
